params.body:
## Why

The reader moved one page at a time, back or forward. The line under the page only showed how far along the reader was. Reaching the source list at the back of a 28-page report took 27 presses, and going back to a page seen earlier meant counting.

## What

The line under the page is now one mark per page, with one more for the end.

- The marks up to the open page are filled, so the line still shows where the reader is.
- A mark takes the reader to its page.
- While the pointer or the keyboard focus is on a mark, the page it stands for is named above the track ("Page 8", "End").
- The room to press is taller than the mark itself, so it works with a finger.

The arrows, the arrow keys and swiping work as before.

## Checked

- `FullReportReaderTest`: a report of twelve pages has thirteen marks, each going to its own page, named for screen readers.
- Opened in a browser against a local copy with a nine-page preview, at 1400 and at 390 wide: a press on the sixth mark opens page 6, and the counter and the filled marks follow.
- Full suite 672 of 673; the one failure is `BuildStampTest`, which needs a git folder the worktree does not have.
params.title: The report reader goes to any page from the track under it
